conviction_note: Evidence is close to balanced: a mid-quarter insider buying cluster, the Academy load-in moved into FQ3 and a $2.3m tariff refund booked to FQ3 COGS sit against the company's silence where it pre-announced every up quarter (FQ3'25, FQ4'25, FQ1'26) but not the -43% FQ2, a falling web-traffic proxy, and a stale-looking FY consensus that any outlook would reset. p_up is 47 (moved toward 50 from 46 because this name sold its pre-announced beats and the bar has a single source) on a 20% abs move rebuilt from full prints only. The findings sum to -0.4 and the scaled number is -1.2; both are small, they agree in sign, and neither is a conviction call.
bar: FQ3 (Jun-Aug 2026) revenue ~$16.0m, EPS -$0.14, whisper -$0.18 (earningswhispers, 2026-09-30, https://earningswhispers.com/article/BYRN/20303). Single source: MarketBeat shows a stale one-analyst $0.11 EPS (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BYRN/earnings/), and an FY consensus of ~$115m on the same earningswhispers page implies a ~$54m Q4. No company guide. Every finding is capped small for that reason. Arithmetic check: $16.0m x 62% GM less ~$15.35m opex (Q2 call: $14.6m base + ~$0.75m/qtr marketing) plus the $2.3m refund gives about -$0.14 on 22.69m shares, so the EPS consensus appears to include the refund already.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.02% of float, 3.87 days to cover (marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BYRN/short-interest, fetched 2026-10-07 by the sweep, settlement date not shown), down from 22.9% in Sept 2025: not crowded. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided, OI 199, put/call OI 0.16), so there is no skew. Run-up is +15.9% over 5d and +5.6% over 20d, at -86% from the 52w high and +19% off the low. Insider cluster buy in late July at $3.42-3.63.

findings.finding: Byrna pre-announced preliminary revenue roughly 5-9 days after quarter end for every recent up quarter (FQ3'25 on 2025-09-04, FQ4'25 on 2025-12-08, FQ1'26 on 2026-03-09, the last under the new CEO). It stayed silent for the -43% FQ2'26 and is silent again for FQ3'26, whose quarter ended 2026-08-31 (EDGAR shows no 8-K 2.02 or 7.01 revenue release since then, only governance items on 09-03 and 09-29).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Full prints with no prior pre-announcement: FQ2'26 (2026-07-09) -33.7%. Pre-announced prints still moved: FQ1'26 -31.0%, FQ4'25 +11.6%, FQ3'25 +21.2%.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-07 (EDGAR list fetched); pattern documented at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/08/3201541/0/en/Byrna-Technologies-Announces-Preliminary-Fiscal-Fourth-Quarter-Revenues-of-35-1-Million-Up-26-From-Fiscal-Q4-2024.html (2025-12-08) and https://www.stocktitan.net/news/BYRN/byrna-technologies-announces-preliminary-fiscal-first-quarter-okbr1ffsqbaz.html (2026-03-09)
findings.why_not_priced: Previews frame the quarter as 'transition' and nobody ties it to the disclosure habit. If the silence were read as a signal of no upside surprise, the +15.9% 5-day run-up into the print would not be there. Partly priced, because the $16m consensus is already flat to Q2.
findings.independence: This is an inference from absence and shares no document with the other findings. The sweep flagged the same gap independently. A new CEO could have changed the policy, which is why it stays small.

findings.finding: On the FQ2 call (2026-07-09) management said Academy Sports' load-in had moved from Q2 into Q3 on Academy's scheduling, holiday load-ins would begin late in Q3, and gross margin should stay 'near or above' the 62% adjusted level. That gives FQ3 sell-in that FQ2 did not have, against a consensus that only holds revenue flat to FQ2 at $16.0m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue is the line this name trades on. FQ2's -43% revenue miss with no guide drew -33.7%. FQ3'25's beat drew +21.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company said it publicly. Last year FQ3 ($28.2m) and FQ2 ($28.5m) were flat, so seasonality alone puts FQ3 at about FQ2's level. A consensus at $16.0m against FQ2's $16.4m therefore gives no credit for the incremental Academy load-in. If that credit were priced, estimates would sit above FQ2.
findings.independence: Academy currently lists Byrna SD and CL kits (https://www.academy.com/p/byrna-sd-kinetic-kit), but that page carries no date for the load-in. The other findings do not use this document.

findings.finding: The FQ2 10-Q discloses that a $2.3m tariff refund was received after 2026-05-31 and will be recorded as a reduction of cost of goods sold in the period received. That puts it in FQ3: about 14 points of reported gross margin on $16m of revenue, or about $0.10/share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior on this line. The $1.1m FQ2 refund was buried in a -33.7% reaction to revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It is likely priced in EPS: the -$0.14 consensus reconciles only if the refund is included. What may not be priced is a headline reported gross margin in the 70s, which could read well on the wire. It has no path to the guide, so it is sized as a fraction of its dollars.
findings.independence: None. This is the company's own filing, and the refund is an IEEPA exposure correlated with other names.

findings.finding: In late July, in the middle of FQ3 and with June-July trading visible to them, CEO Conn Davis (about 22.1k shares on 07-22/23 at $3.46-3.51), Chairman TJ Kennedy (29k), CFO Laurilee Kearnes (2k) and director Chris Reed (8,150 at $3.63) bought stock in the open market. Former CEO Bryan Ganz (9.6%) also bought 52.2k shares on 07-17 (13D/A 2026-09-08).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior cluster is visible in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4s have been public since July, so the purchases are known. What is not priced is the reading that the people who could see June and July order flow bought anyway. The stock has drifted to about $3.79 from the $3.4-3.6 they paid, which is roughly flat, so the market has not rewarded the signal. The dollar amounts are small (about $215k in total).
findings.independence: Ganz's purchases come from a separate filer and document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318455/000121465926011482/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml (2026-09-08).

findings.finding: Similarweb shows byrna.com visits down 16.5% month on month in the latest month, and the global rank slipping to #64,536 from #54,708 over the prior three-month period. The FQ2 call had said traffic was 'fairly consistent from the end of Q2 into the start of Q3', so this points to softer DTC traffic into the holiday-quarter outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ2's weak e-commerce traffic (-13% y/y, conversion 0.59% vs 1.0%) was the core of a -33.7% reaction.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-07 (fetched; the page does not label the month)
findings.why_not_priced: Third-party traffic estimates are not in any preview. The month is unlabelled and September seasonality is unknown, so this is a weak proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy only. FQ2 traffic and conversion were down per the earningswhispers preview (https://earningswhispers.com/article/BYRN/20303), which is a different period.

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue consensus on earningswhispers is about $115m. With H1 at $45.4m and FQ3 at about $16m, that implies a Q4 of about $54m against $35.1m a year ago. Management has said FY26 'will not be a revenue-growth year' and that Q3 is a transition, so any Q4 or FY commentary on the call is likely to force estimate cuts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no formal guide since the CEO change. The no-guide, 'not a growth year' print on 2026-07-09 drew -33.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: At an ~$86m market cap and about 0.7x the FY consensus sales, the price clearly does not believe $115m, so most of a reset is priced. The FY number is probably stale estimates rather than a live bar, and it has one source, so this is capped small under the bar rule.
findings.independence: Same document as the bar. The FQ2 release confirms 'not a revenue-growth year' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001354866/000143774926023101/ex_985847.htm).

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The +15.9% 5-day run-up and the insider buying lean positive, while the disclosure silence and a stale FY bar lean negative. Net, the evidence is close to balanced, which is why p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (single-sourced bar): the FY-consensus guidance finding was capped from -1.0 to -0.7.
Rule 5 (absence and proxies): the no-pre-announcement finding is an inference from absence, so it went from -1.0 to -0.7. The Similarweb proxy went from -0.7 to -0.5 because its month is unlabelled.
Rule 1 (the name sold a pre-announced +11% revenue quarter for -31%): p_up moved from 46 to 47.
'Rebuild the base rate from confirmed releases': the full-print reactions (-33.7, -31.0, +11.6, +21.2, -21.3) give a median of about 21%, so abs_move went from 18 to 20.
Rule 2 (one-off): the tariff refund stays at +0.3. It was already sized as a fraction of its dollars and appears to be in the EPS consensus.
Rule 8: left standing. There is no confirmed, unpriced company-level number here to size up.
